about: Short temperament notes in our own words (not copied from any breed standard), keyed by dex id. traits: three words; text: one or two sentences.

pug.text: A sociable lap dog that loves people and attention. Snores, snuffles and rarely wants a long run.

chihuahua-smooth-coat.text: Tiny but confident, often bonding closely with one person. Quick to bark at strangers.

italian-greyhound.text: A slim, affectionate sighthound that loves warmth and a sprint. Can be shy with strangers.

cavalier-king-charles-spaniel.text: Friendly with everyone, dogs included. Happy on the couch or on a walk.

jack-russell-terrier.text: Small, tireless and always busy. Loves chasing and digging, and needs plenty to do.

staffordshire-bull-terrier.text: Muscular but soft-hearted, famously devoted to its family. Full of energy and keen on a game.

west-highland-white-terrier.text: A bright little terrier with a big personality. Independent, but happy to be in the thick of things.

bull-terrier.text: A comic, strong-willed dog that loves people. Needs firm, fun training and lots of exercise.

labrador-retriever.text: Gentle, food-motivated and keen to please. Loves water, fetch and nearly everyone it meets.

golden-retriever.text: Patient and friendly, great with children. Thrives on company and a daily retrieve.

cocker-spaniel.text: A happy, tail-wagging gundog that loves to sniff and explore. Gentle and keen to please.

hungarian-vizsla.text: Known as a velcro dog: it sticks close to its people. Needs lots of running every day.

whippet.text: Calm and cuddly at home, a sprinter in the park. Quiet and polite with other dogs.

rhodesian-ridgeback.text: Calm and reserved with strangers, devoted at home. Strong and athletic, with a mind of its own.

dachshund.text: Brave and curious, with a big bark for its size. Loves to burrow, sniff and be with its people.

beagle.text: A sociable pack hound led by its nose. Food-mad and vocal, with a famous baying howl.

australian-cattle-dog.text: Smart, tough and protective of its people. Bred to work all day, so it needs a job and lots of exercise.

border-collie.text: Often called the smartest breed. Needs daily work, play or training to stay happy.

german-shepherd-dog.text: Steady, protective and very trainable. Bonds closely with its family and is wary of strangers.

boxer.text: Bouncy and fun-loving, a great family dog. Stays puppyish for years and loves a romp.

bernese-mountain-dog.text: A gentle giant that's devoted to its family. Easygoing at home and loves cool weather.

schnauzer-miniature.text: Bright and chatty, a keen watchdog. Small, sturdy and happy to join any activity.

french-bulldog.text: A cheerful companion that's happy in an apartment. Needs only short walks and dislikes the heat.

dalmatian.text: Lively and athletic, bred to run with carriages. Needs plenty of exercise and company.

british-bulldog.text: Calm, kind and a little stubborn. Prefers short strolls and a comfy spot over long runs.

cavoodle.text: Usually sweet and sociable like a Cavalier, and clever like a Poodle. A popular family and apartment dog.

groodle.text: Often has a Golden Retriever's friendliness and a Poodle's brains. Needs good daily exercise.

miniature-fox-terrier.text: A quick, keen little dog bred to catch rats. Affectionate at home and always on the lookout.
